about: Hand-written horror definitions. The generator merges each with the members it is planted in and the facts it keys there, and writes horrors/H-*.json. Edit this file to change a horror's description or citations; edit generator/apps/ to change where and how it is planted. Never edit horrors/ or key/ by hand.

horrors.title: A cols 1-6 sequence number read as the operand of a verb whose operand is on the next line
shapes: PERFORM / <procedure-name> on the next line
GO TO / <procedure-name> on the next line (inside IF ... END-IF)
CALL / '<literal>' on the next line
CALL / <identifier> on the next line
COPY / <member>. on the next line
horrors.asserts: The operand is the word on the next line, never that line's sequence number: the edges, the CALL sites and the COPY edge name the real procedure, program and member, and no edge, call site or import names a sequence number.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: The content of this area can consist of any character in the character set of the computer.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: literal-1 or the contents of identifier-1 must specify the program-name of the called subprogram.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: A COPY statement can appear in the source text anywhere a character string or a separator can appear.

horrors.notes: The sequence number area is outside the program text, so a statement may continue onto the next line at any separator. The phantoms name the exact sequence number the engine would read (the next line's cols 1-6).

horrors.title: A paragraph cut at a conditional or non-terminating GOBACK / RETURN / EXIT
shapes: EXEC CICS / RETURN TRANSID(...) / END-EXEC inside IF ... END-IF, more statements after it (CUSTINQ 0000-MAIN)
a paragraph whose name starts with RETURN (CUSTINQ RETURN-TO-MENU)
EXIT PERFORM inside an inline PERFORM, more statements after the loop: unnumbered (CUSTINQ 4000-FIND-BLANK) and numbered (ACCTRPT 2500-SCAN-HISTORY)
PL/I: IF CLM_AMT > 0 THEN ... ELSE RETURN; then CALL LOG_CLAIM / WRITE_CLAIM in CHECK_CLAIM (CLMPROC)
horrors.asserts: A paragraph runs from its header to just before the next paragraph or section header; the key's end_line is the last code line before that header. Every PERFORM after the conditional terminator belongs to the paragraph.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: A paragraph ends immediately before the next paragraph-name or section header, or at the end of the PROCEDURE DIVISION.

citations.doc: CICS Transaction Server for z/OS 6.x
citations.quote: RETURN returns control from an application program either to an application program at the next higher logical level, or to CICS.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: The EXIT statement ... provides a way to exit from a section, a paragraph, or an inline PERFORM statement.

citations.doc: Enterprise PL/I for z/OS 6.1 Language Reference (SC31-5716-00)
citations.quote: The RETURN statement terminates execution of the subroutine or function procedure that contains the RETURN statement and returns control to the invoking procedure.

horrors.notes: In a numbered member the engine's line-leading terminator test does not see EXIT behind the sequence number, so the numbered plant can pass for the wrong reason; the unnumbered plants exercise the cut.

horrors.title: Main-line statements between PROCEDURE DIVISION and the first paragraph belong to no unit
shapes: OPEN / PERFORM ... THRU / PERFORM ... UNTIL / GOBACK right after PROCEDURE DIVISION, before the first paragraph name (ACCTPOST)
horrors.asserts: The main line is a unit (kind mainline, no name) from the first statement after the PROCEDURE DIVISION header to the line before the first paragraph; its PERFORM targets are edges from it. The scorer accepts a function_data unit or a synthetic_unit_data row there.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: If there are no declaratives (format 2), a paragraph-name is not required in the PROCEDURE DIVISION.

horrors.title: A COPY that does not start its line draws no import
shapes: 01  WS-RPT-HEAD.  COPY RPTHDR.
01  WS-RPT-TOTALS.  COPY RPTTOT. COPY RPTCNT. (two COPYs on one line)
horrors.asserts: Each COPY is an import of its member, resolved to the copybook in the app's library, at the line of its 01.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: A COPY statement can appear in the source text anywhere a character string or a separator can appear. ... Each COPY statement must be preceded by a space and ended with a separator period.

horrors.title: EXEC SQL CALL of a stored procedure recorded as a COBOL dynamic CALL
shapes: EXEC SQL / CALL PRODPROC.CUSTBAL / (:CUST-ID, :CUST-BAL) / END-EXEC (schema-qualified, multi-line)
EXEC SQL CALL CUSTAUDT END-EXEC (unqualified, one line)
horrors.asserts: Both are SQL statements with verb CALL and the procedure name; neither is a COBOL CALL site or a call edge.

citations.doc: Db2 13 for z/OS SQL Reference
citations.quote: The CALL statement invokes a stored procedure. ... This statement can be embedded in an application program.

horrors.title: Inline PERFORM headers and EXIT PERFORM read as PERFORM targets
shapes: PERFORM TEST AFTER VARYING ... (WITH omitted)
PERFORM TEST BEFORE UNTIL ...
PERFORM WS-N TIMES ... END-PERFORM (inline, identifier count)
PERFORM 3 TIMES ... END-PERFORM (inline, literal count)
IF ... EXIT PERFORM END-IF
PERFORM 3100-FORMAT-TOTAL 2 TIMES (out-of-line: a real edge, the control case)
horrors.asserts: An inline PERFORM names no procedure, so it draws no edge; EXIT PERFORM is not a PERFORM. Out-of-line PERFORM procedure-name n TIMES is an edge to the procedure.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: The PERFORM statement is an out-of-line PERFORM statement, when procedure-name-1 is specified. ... The PERFORM statement is an inline PERFORM statement, when procedure-name-1 is omitted.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: The EXIT statement ... provides a way to exit from a section, a paragraph, or an inline PERFORM statement.

horrors.notes: PERFORM FOREVER (#4305's GnuCOBOL / Micro Focus form) is not planted: it is not Enterprise COBOL, and this estate is IBM dialect. Its IBM counterpart, PERFORM UNTIL EXIT, is a phase-1 candidate.

horrors.title: IDMS IDMS-CONTROL SECTION / PROTOCOL (ENVIRONMENT DIVISION) recorded as procedure units
shapes: ENVIRONMENT DIVISION. IDMS-CONTROL SECTION. PROTOCOL. MODE IS IDMS-DC DEBUG IDMS-RECORDS MANUAL. (LNIDMS01, numbered)
DATA DIVISION. SCHEMA SECTION. DB LOANSS01 WITHIN LOANSCHM. (LNIDMS01): not in #4306, found by this crucible
horrors.asserts: Units come from the PROCEDURE DIVISION only: IDMS-CONTROL, PROTOCOL and SCHEMA are not units; the program's three paragraphs are.

citations.doc: Broadcom CA IDMS 19.0 DML Reference for COBOL
citations.quote: An IDMS-CONTROL SECTION is required in the ENVIRONMENT DIVISION to establish the following: Operating mode, Debug sequencing, Variable storage allocation

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: A paragraph ends immediately before the next paragraph-name or section header, or at the end of the PROCEDURE DIVISION.

horrors.notes: IDMS is a Broadcom product, so its rule is cited from Broadcom's documentation. The member is IBM-only (not compiled): GnuCOBOL has no IDMS precompiler. The SCHEMA SECTION shape is reported on #4306.

horrors.title: PROGRAM-ID not recorded when its separator period is missing
shapes: PROGRAM-ID.    LNRATE + blanks to col 72, no period after the name (LNRATE)
PROGRAM-ID LNCALC. (no period after the keyword) (LNCALC)
horrors.asserts: The program-name is LNRATE / LNCALC: PROGRAM-ID names the program whatever the punctuation around it.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference
citations.quote: program-name ... identifies your program

horrors.lower_confidence: IBM's syntax diagram shows both periods as required. That Enterprise COBOL compiles the period-less forms with a diagnostic rests on #4307's evidence (cobol-programming-course CBLDB22 compiles in its own JCL), not on an IBM sentence. The fact the key asserts, the program-name, does not depend on it. Both members are IBM-only here; the check compiles a variant with the periods restored.
horrors.notes: LNRATE has no AUTHOR paragraph, as #4307's CBLDB22 has none: when a period-terminated AUTHOR. line follows the period-less PROGRAM-ID, the engine records the name, which would hide shape 1.

horrors.title: The last DATA DIVISION entry takes its USAGE from the PROCEDURE DIVISION
shapes: 01 WS-MSG PIC X(40). as the last WORKING-STORAGE entry, DISPLAY WS-MSG in the procedure (ACCTUPD)
01 WS-LEN PIC 9(4). as the last entry, MOVE 'BINARY' TO WS-MODE in the procedure (BILLCALC): the engine sizes WS-LEN 2 bytes, not 4
horrors.asserts: A data description entry ends at its separator period: an entry with no USAGE clause has no usage (DISPLAY by default, 4 bytes for PIC 9(4)). Every other program's last entry is marked depends_on H-0009.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A separator period is composed of a period followed by a space.

horrors.title: A COPY of a member holding its own 01 is folded into the copy_members of the 01 above it
shapes: 01 WS-COMMAREA. / COPY CUSTCOMM. / COPY CUSTMS. / COPY DFHAID. (CUSTINQ; DFHAID is outside the estate)
01 WS-INV-AREA. / COPY INVCOMM. / COPY INVMSG. where INVMSG holds its own 01 (INVUPD)
horrors.asserts: A level-01 entry in copied text begins a new record: the 01 above it holds only the first COPY's entries.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.section: Levels of data in a record description entry (p.167)
citations.quote: 01 This level-number specifies the record itself, and is the most inclusive level-number possible.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.section: Levels of data in a record description entry (p.167)
citations.quote: A group item includes all group and elementary items that follow it until a level-number less than or equal to the level-number of that group is encountered.

horrors.title: A GDG relative generation (+1) / (-1) is captured as a truncated DSN
shapes: DSN=PROD.ACCT.MASTER(+1) (ACCTPRC)
DSN=PROD.BILL.MASTER(0) / (-1) / (+1) in one step (BILLMTH)
DSN=PROD.PAYR.REGISTER(+1) (PAYWKLY)
horrors.asserts: A DD names the GDG base and a relative generation; the dataset reference is the base, with or without its generation, never a name cut at the sign.

citations.doc: z/OS V2R2 MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385-03)
citations.section: DD statement: DSNAME parameter, cataloged data set name (p.178-179)
citations.quote: dsname(generation) Specifies the name of a generation data group (GDG) and the generation number (zero or a signed integer) of a generation data set within the GDG.

citations.doc: z/OS V2R2 DFSMS Using Data Sets (SC23-6855-03)
citations.quote: The relative name is a signed integer used to refer to the latest (0), the next to the latest (-1), and so forth, generation.

horrors.title: A sequence-numbered blank line extends the previous unit's extent
shapes: empty numbered lines (cols 1-6 only) between BILLCALC's paragraphs
horrors.asserts: A line with nothing in cols 7-72 holds no code: a paragraph's extent ends at its last code line, whatever cols 1-6 hold.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: The content of this area can consist of any character in the character set of the computer.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A paragraph ends immediately before the next paragraph-name or section header, or at the end of the PROCEDURE DIVISION.

horrors.title: Columns 73-80 identification text on paragraph lines
shapes: identification text GL000100 / GL002000 in cols 73-80 of every line of two GLPOST paragraphs, including their headers
horrors.asserts: Cols 73-80 are outside the program text: the paragraphs, their PERFORM edges and extents are what cols 1-72 say.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: Reference format consists of the following areas in a 72-character line.

horrors.notes: IBM's 6.4 Language Reference defines a 72-character line and does not describe cols 73-80 for source; the compiler ignores them.

horrors.title: Record copybook: level-01 elementary items, REDEFINES, nested groups, change markers in cols 1-6
shapes: BILREC: two 01 records (one elementary), nested 05/10/15 groups, a REDEFINES group, change marker BL0412 in cols 1-6 of two entries
horrors.asserts: Every entry is a data item at its level, under its parent, whatever cols 1-6 hold; the elementary 01 is a record of its own.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: The content of this area can consist of any character in the character set of the computer.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.section: Levels of data in a record description entry (p.167)
citations.quote: A group item includes all group and elementary items that follow it until a level-number less than or equal to the level-number of that group is encountered.

horrors.title: A DCLGEN member (.dcl) is a COBOL / SQL member to scan
shapes: DCLCUST.dcl and DCLINVT.dcl in the app's dclgen library: DECLARE TABLE plus the host structure
horrors.asserts: A DCLGEN member's DECLARE TABLE columns and its COBOL host structure are facts of that member.

citations.doc: Db2 13 for z/OS Commands
citations.quote: The declarations generator (DCLGEN) produces an SQL DECLARE TABLE statement and a COBOL, PL/I, or C data declaration for a table or a view named in the catalog.

horrors.title: COPY forms: REPLACING ==pseudo-text==, a quoted text-name, IN library
shapes: COPY PAYTPL REPLACING ==:TAG:== BY ==EMP==. (the copybook's :TAG:- names are not data-names)
COPY 'PAYCON'. (a literal text-name)
COPY DATEWS IN SHRCPY. (a library-name)
horrors.asserts: REPLACING applies before the entries exist: WS-EMP holds EMP-ID / EMP-NAME / EMP-RATE (40 bytes); the copybook's own :TAG: entries are not data-names. A quoted text-name and IN library resolve like the plain forms.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: The COPY statement with REPLACING phrase can be used to replace parts of words, either by using the LEADING|TRAILING partial-word-1 BY partial-word-2 phrase, or by using the pseudo-text :TAG: or (TAG) method.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: Latin uppercase letters A through Z, Latin lowercase letters a through z, digits 0 through 9, - (hyphen), _ (underscore)

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: literal-1, literal-2 Must be alphanumeric literals. literal-1 identifies the copy text. literal-2 identifies where the copy text exists.

horrors.title: A one-line EXEC SQL INCLUDE member END-EXEC
shapes: EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA END-EXEC. and EXEC SQL INCLUDE DCLCUST END-EXEC. on one line each (CUSTDBIO, INVDB)
horrors.asserts: Each INCLUDE is an import of its member (SQLCA is Db2-supplied: no member in the estate).

citations.doc: Db2 13 for z/OS SQL Reference
citations.quote: The INCLUDE statement inserts application code, including declarations and statements, into a source program.

horrors.title: A data-only copybook (no procedure code, 60+ lines) is still an import target
shapes: INVITEM: 60+ lines of data entries and nothing else, COPYed by INVUPD
horrors.asserts: A copybook with no procedure code is still a member the program imports; its entries are data items.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A COPY statement can appear in the source text anywhere a character string or a separator can appear.

horrors.title: PROGRAM-ID. alone on its line, the name on the next (numbered)
shapes: 000200 PROGRAM-ID. / 000300     GLPOST. in a numbered member
horrors.asserts: The program-name is GLPOST, the next word after the PROGRAM-ID paragraph header, never the next line's sequence number.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A user-defined word or alphanumeric literal, but not a figurative constant, that identifies your program.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: The content of this area can consist of any character in the character set of the computer.

horrors.title: A paragraph header whose separator period is on the next line
shapes: 1100-OPEN-MSG alone on its line, the separator period alone on the next (GLPOST)
horrors.asserts: 1100-OPEN-MSG is a paragraph from its name to its last code line.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A space can immediately precede or follow any separator except: The opening pseudo-text delimiter ... Within quotation marks.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: If there is no hyphen (-) in the indicator area (column 7) of a line, the last character of the preceding line is assumed to be followed by a space.

horrors.lower_confidence: No IBM sentence states outright that a paragraph-name's separator period may be on the next line; it follows from the separator and continuation rules (an end of line is a space; a space may precede a separator period). GnuCOBOL -std=ibm accepts it.

horrors.title: Commented-out CALL / PERFORM (indicator *) are not statements
shapes: *    CALL 'OLDINVAD' USING WS-INV-AREA and *    PERFORM 2500-OLD-REORDER as comment lines (INVUPD)
horrors.asserts: A comment line holds no statement: no call site, no edge.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A comment line is any line with an asterisk (*) or slash (/) in the indicator area (column 7) of the line, or with a floating comment indicator (*>) as the first character-string in the program text area (Area A plus Area B).

horrors.title: SPECIAL-NAMES / I-O-CONTROL are not units; all-digit paragraph names are
shapes: SPECIAL-NAMES. C01 IS TOP-OF-PAGE. and I-O-CONTROL. APPLY WRITE-ONLY ON PAY-FILE. (PAYMAIN)
all-digit paragraph names 0100. / 0200.
horrors.asserts: SPECIAL-NAMES and I-O-CONTROL are ENVIRONMENT DIVISION paragraphs, not units; 0100 and 0200 are paragraphs.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: The SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph is the name of an ENVIRONMENT DIVISION paragraph in which environment-names are related to user-specified mnemonic-names.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: Most user-defined words (all except section-names, paragraph-names, priority-numbers, and level-numbers) must contain at least one alphabetic character.

horrors.title: A spaced-out PROCEDURE        DIVISION header and an inline paragraph header
shapes: PROCEDURE        DIVISION. (multiple spaces, GLPOST)
1000-INIT. MOVE ZERO TO WS-TOTAL (the first statement on the header line)
horrors.asserts: The procedure division starts at the spaced header; 1000-INIT is a paragraph whose first statement shares its header line.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: Anywhere a space is used as a separator or as part of a separator, more than one space can be used.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A paragraph ends immediately before the next paragraph-name or section header, or at the end of the PROCEDURE DIVISION.

horrors.title: A called program also named in a CSD group and as a JCL job resolves to the COBOL source
shapes: EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('CUSTDBIO'), CUSTDBIO also DEFINEd in CSD group CUSTGRP
EXEC CICS LINK PROGRAM('INVDB'), INVDB also a CSD PROGRAM and the name of a JCL job
horrors.asserts: The LINK target is the COBOL program whose PROGRAM-ID is that name, not the CSD deck or the job.

citations.doc: CICS Transaction Server for z/OS 6.x
citations.quote: PROGRAM resources control information for a program that is stored in the program library and used to process a transaction, or part of a transaction.

citations.doc: CICS Transaction Server for z/OS 6.x
citations.quote: LINK passes control from an application program at one logical level to an application program at the next lower logical level.

horrors.title: SIGN LEADING / TRAILING SEPARATE takes a byte of its own
shapes: 05 WS-ADJUST PIC S9(7)V99 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE (10 bytes)
05 WS-CREDIT PIC S9(5) SIGN TRAILING SEPARATE (6 bytes)
horrors.asserts: With SEPARATE CHARACTER the sign takes its own byte: the layout counts it.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: The character S in the PICTURE character string is counted in determining the size of the data item (in terms of standard data format characters).

horrors.title: A paragraph named END-xxx (END-IPROC1) is a paragraph
shapes: paragraph END-IPROC1. PERFORMed from 0000-MAIN (GLPOST)
horrors.asserts: END-IPROC1 is a user-defined word, so a legal paragraph-name; only the reserved END-xxx words are scope terminators.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: Most user-defined words (all except section-names, paragraph-names, priority-numbers, and level-numbers) must contain at least one alphabetic character.

horrors.title: A mixed-case paragraph name (End-Program) is a paragraph
shapes: paragraph End-Program. (mixed case), PERFORM End-Program (GLPOST)
horrors.asserts: End-Program is a paragraph; COBOL words are not case-sensitive.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: Latin uppercase letters A through Z, Latin lowercase letters a through z, digits 0 through 9, - (hyphen), _ (underscore)

horrors.title: Free-format source: indented level numbers are data entries, not paragraphs
shapes: >>SOURCE FORMAT FREE, data entries indented under their parents (    01 VALUE-BYTES.) (MODRATE)
paragraph LOOKUP-RATE. starting in column 1, its hyphen in column 7: not in #4203, found by this crucible
horrors.asserts: In free format there are no columns: indented level numbers are data entries, and LOOKUP-RATE is one paragraph-name.

citations.doc: GnuCOBOL 3.x Programmer's Guide
citations.quote: in this mode of operation, COBOL statements may each be up to 255 characters long, with no specific requirements as to what should appear in which columns.

horrors.notes: Not IBM dialect: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 has only the 72-column reference format, and IBM COBOL for Linux needs a conversion utility for free-format source. The member stands for code rehosted off z/OS and is compiled by GnuCOBOL (-std=ibm accepts the directive).

horrors.title: A PROGRAM-ID written as a literal ('PAYRPT')
shapes: PROGRAM-ID. 'PAYRPT'. starting in column 9, and END PROGRAM 'PAYRPT'.
horrors.asserts: The program-name is PAYRPT.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A user-defined word or alphanumeric literal, but not a figurative constant, that identifies your program.

horrors.title: An unnamed data description entry is an implicit FILLER
shapes: 05 PIC X(6) VALUE 'BILL: ' and 05 PIC X(2) VALUE SPACES inside WS-PRINT-LINE (BILLCALC)
horrors.asserts: An entry with no data-name is FILLER: it is a data item named FILLER with its picture, and it occupies storage.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: If data-name-1 or the FILLER clause is omitted, the data item being described is treated as though FILLER had been specified.

horrors.title: Several programs in one member: nested and batch-compiled siblings, each with MAINLINE SECTION
shapes: PAYMAIN holds PAYCALC (nested, END PROGRAM PAYCALC) and is followed by the batch-compiled sibling 'PAYRPT'; each program opens with MAINLINE SECTION
each program's own WORKING-STORAGE; CALL 'PAYCALC' / CALL 'PAYRPT' resolve inside the member
horrors.asserts: Each program has its own units, data items and entry point; a CALL of a nested or sibling program resolves to this member.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.section: COBOL program structure; End program markers (p.57, p.84-85)
citations.quote: A COBOL program can contain other COBOL programs, which in turn can contain still other COBOL programs. These contained programs are called nested programs.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.section: End program, end class, and end method markers (p.57)
citations.quote: An end program marker separates each program in the sequence of programs.

horrors.title: ASSIGN TO at the end of a line with cols 73-80 identification; the assignment-name on the next line
shapes: SELECT JRNL-FILE ASSIGN TO + GL001000 in cols 73-80; the assignment-name JRNLIN on the next line, also tagged
horrors.asserts: The assignment-name is JRNLIN: cols 73-80 are outside the line and the clause continues in Area B of the next.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: Reference format consists of the following areas in a 72-character line.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: Any sentence, entry, clause, or phrase that requires more than one line can be continued in Area B of the next line that is neither a comment line nor a blank line.

horrors.title: PERFORM UNTIL EXIT (an inline loop left only by EXIT PERFORM)
shapes: PERFORM UNTIL EXIT ... IF WS-I > 12 EXIT PERFORM END-IF ... END-PERFORM, then PERFORM 2000-ROUND (PAYCALC)
horrors.asserts: An inline loop: no edge from its header; the PERFORM after it belongs to the paragraph.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: If the UNTIL phrase with the EXIT reserved word is specified, execution proceeds exactly as if the same PERFORM statement were coded with condition-1 specified, except that condition-1 never evaluates as true.

horrors.notes: New in Enterprise COBOL 6.4 (Summary of changes: PERFORM ... UNTIL EXIT support); it does not compile on 6.3 or earlier. No gitgalaxy issue: an IBM dialect corner planted ahead of any defect.

horrors.title: Same-named copybook in two libraries: SYSLIB order picks the app's own
shapes: DATEWS in PAYRCPY (18 bytes, ISO date) and in SHRCPY (16 bytes): PAYMAIN's plain COPY DATEWS takes PAYR's, COPY DATEWS IN SHRCPY the shared one
ACCTPOST and CUSTINQ COPY DATEWS: their SYSLIB has no PAYRCPY, so the shared one (depends_on H-0034)
horrors.asserts: COPY searches the program's own library concatenation and the first library holding the member wins; a library-name restricts the search to that library.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: If no library name is specified in the COPY statement, the concatenation of datasets allocated to the SYSLIB ddname is searched.

citations.doc: z/OS V2R2 DFSMS Using Data Sets (SC23-6855-03)
citations.quote: If two members of different data sets in the concatenation have the same name, the FIND macro determines the address of the first one in the concatenation.

horrors.title: Raw EBCDIC members as 80-byte records with no line ends (a binary PDS transfer)
shapes: KØBREG: cp277 (Denmark / Norway), FB80, the program's every fact keyed as for a UTF-8 member

COPY　KYUYCPY. (a copybook stored as UTF-8 with a BOM)
horrors.asserts: A full-width space separates words exactly as a space does: the entry, its picture, the division header and the COPY are read.

citations.quote: The EBCDIC DBCS space character has the value X'4040', the national space character has the value NX'0020', and the UTF-8 space character has the value UX'20'.

horrors.lower_confidence: Not IBM: Enterprise COBOL separates words with single-byte spaces. The member stands for opensourcecobol4j code; the dialect's rule is evidenced by its own test suite (via #3956), not by a language reference.

horrors.title: Full-width hyphens and digits in names; names that must not collide

SECTION Ｓ−初期化 and paragraph 初期化１ (a full-width digit)
horrors.asserts: Full-width hyphens and digits are characters of the word: the three items stay three items, and Ｓ−初期化 is a section.

horrors.lower_confidence: U+2212 (MINUS SIGN) is not the DBCS hyphen IBM means (U+FF0D); it is planted because opensourcecobol4j estates carry it (#3991).

horrors.title: DBCS in EBCDIC: SO/SI-delimited words, mixed and G literals, unbalanced and nested shift codes in comments
shapes: KYUYO01 (cp930, FB80): data names 処理件数 / 見出し / 漢字欄, sections and paragraphs 主処理 / 開始 / 集計
VALUE '給与明細ABC' (mixed literal, shift codes paired)
VALUE G'漢字欄名' (DBCS literal)
comment lines with a Shift-Out never shifted back in, and with two Shift-Outs nested
SHAINREC (cp939, NEL): 社員名 PIC G(10) (20 bytes)
horrors.asserts: Every DBCS run reads as its characters, each record starts in single-byte mode whatever the previous one left, and a PIC G / PIC N item takes 2 bytes per character.

horrors.title: DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, with VALUE 1,50 in a copybook

horrors.asserts: The comparison and the PERFORM under it are facts like any other; what they mean depends on the collating sequence.

horrors.notes: #3988 trap 4. No scanner channel records a collating sequence: this horror's facts are structural, and the trap is for translators (a Java port comparing as Unicode). It is planted so the estate carries it.
